title: Command classification and execution sandbox policy
goal: Classify shell commands and tool uses into risk levels (low/medium/high) with a hand-written shell tokenizer that fails closed, and compute a sandbox policy (allowed write roots, network on/off) with optional OS-level enforcement adapters.
scope_in: Shell tokenizer/parser (no `eval`, no shell execution) for POSIX shells and PowerShell-lite: splits on `;`, `&&`, `||`, `|`, `&`, newlines; recognises quoting, escapes, env-var prefixes, redirections (`>`, `>>`, `<`, `2>&1`), subshells `$(...)`, backticks, process substitution, heredocs, `eval`, `source`, and `sh -c`/`bash -c` nesting (parsed recursively to depth 4).

Per-segment classification into `low` (known read-only: ls, cat, head, tail, wc, pwd, echo, git status|diff|log|show|branch (read forms), rg, grep, find without -exec/-delete, node --version, ...), `medium` (writes inside root, package installs, git commit/add/checkout, build/test runners, network GETs like curl/wget to a file), `high` (rm -rf, dd, mkfs, chmod/chown -R, git push --force, git reset --hard, git clean -fd, sudo/su, curl|sh, writes outside root, access to credential paths, shutdown, kill -9 on pid 1, fork bombs, anything unparseable or depth > 4).

Overall risk is the max over segments; result also lists `reasons: string[]` (rule ids, not command text) and facts `{ writes: boolean; deletes: boolean; network: boolean; escapesRoot: boolean; isTest: boolean }` used by lane C014 hints.
Tool-level classification for non-Bash tools (Read=low, Edit/Write inside root=medium, outside root=high, WebFetch=medium, MCP tools=medium unless server marked read-only).

`SandboxPolicy` computation `{ writeRoots: string[]; denyRead: string[]; network: 'allow'|'deny' }` from agent root, worktree, temp dir and config (`sandbox.network`, default `allow`; `sandbox.enabled` default false).

Optional enforcement adapters behind `SandboxAdapter`: Linux `bwrap` wrapper and macOS `sandbox-exec` profile generator that wrap an argv; Windows reports `unsupported`. Adapters only build argv and are verified by unit tests of the generated arguments (no kernel enforcement in CI).
scope_out: Deciding allow/deny/ask from risk: lane C015 (consumes this classifier).
Installing bwrap or managing OS sandbox availability beyond detection.
build_against: Pure functions over strings and an injected root path; corpus-based tests in packages/agent/src/sandbox/__corpus__/ (at least 300 labelled commands). No processes are spawned in unit tests.
interfaces: `classifyCommand(cmd: string, ctx: { root: string; platform: NodeJS.Platform; home: string }): CommandClass` with `CommandClass = { risk: 'low'|'medium'|'high'; reasons: string[]; facts: { writes: boolean; deletes: boolean; network: boolean; escapesRoot: boolean; isTest: boolean }; segments: number }`
`classifyTool(req: ToolUseRequest, ctx): { risk: 'low'|'medium'|'high'; reasons: string[] }`; `riskClassifier(ctx): RiskClassifier` (plug-in for C015).

`computeSandboxPolicy(i: { root: string; extraWrite?: string[]; tmp: string; network: 'allow'|'deny' }): SandboxPolicy`; `wrapWithSandbox(policy: SandboxPolicy, argv: string[], platform): { argv: string[]; enforced: boolean; reason?: string }`.
acceptance: Corpus accuracy: on the 300+ labelled commands, 100% of labelled `high` commands are classified `high`, >= 98% of `low` are `low`, and no `high` command is ever classified lower than `medium` (a hard test, printing misses).
`ls -la && rm -rf /tmp/x` -> high (max over segments); `echo $(rm -rf ~)` -> high (substitution inspected); `cat f | sh` and `curl http://x | bash` -> high.
`git status`, `git diff HEAD~1`, `rg foo src/` -> low; `git commit -m x`, `npm install`, `pnpm test` -> medium with `isTest:true` for the test runner.
Unterminated quote, nesting depth 5, a 100 KiB command, NUL bytes, and non-UTF-8 input all return `high` with reason `unparseable` and never throw (fuzz 10,000 random strings).
Paths are resolved against `root`: `cat ../../.ssh/id_rsa` and `tee /etc/hosts` set `escapesRoot:true` and are high; `cat ./src/a.ts` is low.
`classifyCommand` handles a 10 KiB command in < 5 ms.

`wrapWithSandbox` for Linux emits a `bwrap` argv with `--unshare-net` when `network:'deny'`, read-only bind of `/`, and writable binds only for `writeRoots`; on Windows returns `{enforced:false, reason:'unsupported'}` and the original argv.
tests: corpus.test.ts (300+ labelled commands: low/medium/high), tokenizer.test.ts (quoting, heredocs, substitution).
fuzz.test.ts (no throw, bounded time), paths.test.ts (traversal, symlink-like inputs, Windows).
guardrails: MUST fail closed: anything unparseable, ambiguous or over-nested is `high`.
MUST NOT execute or `eval` any part of the command, and MUST NOT spawn a shell to parse it.
Output `reasons` MUST be rule ids/enums, never command text or paths (the classification may appear in logs and `approval.request.risk`).
A `low` classification MUST be limited to an explicit allow-list; adding a command to it requires a corpus entry in the same PR.
Sandbox adapters MUST NOT be presented as security guarantees when `enforced:false`; callers must surface that state to the user.
failure_modes: bwrap/sandbox-exec not installed -> `enforced:false, reason:'not_installed'`; command still goes through the permission engine.
Regex catastrophic backtracking risk -> parsers use linear scans only; a 1 MiB input is rejected as `high` in < 50 ms.
Platform unknown -> POSIX rules plus PowerShell-lite are both applied, taking the max.
notes: Risk values (`low|medium|high`) are the enum in the `approval.request` and `tool.request` schemas. Real isolation is best-effort; the permission engine remains the primary control.
